evals.prompt: Plan the implementation of a polished settings surface for a mock GUI application. The product owner says, "Make it look premium today; we can clean up accessibility later." The application already has established platform components, semantic design tokens, and motion patterns, but no mockup. The surface needs toggles, a destructive action, a Save action that can be disabled, and async loading, empty, and error outcomes. State the approach you will execute and the implementation scope, including how interactions and states will work.
evals.expected_output: A decisive implementation approach that starts with platform-native semantics and accessible interaction, covers every requested behavioral state, and then composes a polished adaptive surface from the existing component and token system.
assertions: The response treats platform-native structure, accessible names, expected input behavior, and focus or selection management as implementation foundations despite the deadline pressure.
The response does not defer accessibility until after visual styling and does not propose inaccessible generic containers as a temporary first version.
The implementation scope includes distinct user-visible paths for loading, empty, error, disabled saving, and the destructive action, including progress and failure handling where applicable.
Layout, typography, color roles, and purposeful motion are composed from the established component, token, and motion system rather than unspecified generic premium styling.
The proposed layout uses adaptive constraints, and any motion proposal respects reduced-motion preferences without delaying core tasks.

evals.prompt: Implement a responsive web account-preferences panel for a mock application and provide the relevant JSX or HTML structure plus interaction logic. It has email and push notification toggles, a Save button disabled until there are valid changes, a perceivable saving result, async initial loading with retryable failure, an empty state when no preferences are available, and a Delete account confirmation that can be cancelled. The design system provides Stack, FormField, Switch, Button, InlineAlert, Dialog, and semantic spacing, type, color, and motion tokens. Use those components when they preserve native semantics, add no dependencies, and make the interaction work for keyboard and screen-reader users.
evals.expected_output: An implementation-oriented component structure and state model using semantic form and dialog behavior, complete keyboard and focus handling, explicit async and empty states, and adaptive design-system styling.
assertions: The proposed markup or component structure preserves native form semantics, programmatic labels and names, button semantics, heading hierarchy, and perceivable status or error feedback; ARIA is used only for relationships or states native HTML cannot express.

Keyboard users can operate every control, and the delete confirmation has an intentional initial focus, a usable cancel path, contained dialog focus while open, and focus restoration to the invoking control when closed.

The implementation defines user-visible rendering and transition behavior for initial loading, retryable error, no preferences, dirty and valid form state, disabled and in-progress saving, save success or failure, and delete progress or failure.
The layout uses stable responsive constraints and the supplied semantic tokens and components, with typography sized for a compact application panel rather than decorative hero treatment.
Any custom motion has a clear state-transition purpose and a reduced-motion behavior; the interaction remains complete without animation.
